patterns.name: Full Intrusion Chain (Recon to Execution to Persistence)
patterns.description: A broader four-stage progression: host fingerprinting and process enumeration, followed by encoded PowerShell execution and registry-based persistence.

patterns.name: Phishing/PowerShell to Registry Persistence
patterns.description: Initial execution via encoded PowerShell followed by registry-based persistence, consistent with a phishing payload establishing a foothold.

patterns.name: Execution to Credential Access to Discovery to Lateral Movement
patterns.description: A staged intrusion progressing from code execution through credential access, host/network discovery, and an attempt at lateral movement.

patterns.name: Compromise to Scheduled Task to Command Execution to Data Staging
patterns.description: Persistence established via scheduled task, followed by command execution and preparation of data for exfiltration.

patterns.name: Reconnaissance Sweep (System, Process, and Network Discovery)
patterns.description: Sequential host and network enumeration -- system information gathering, running-process enumeration, and an outbound connectivity probe -- consistent with an attacker mapping the environment before further action.

patterns.name: Evasion Preparation (Hidden Extensions to Encoded Execution)
patterns.description: File-extension hiding followed by an encoded PowerShell execution, consistent with an attacker preparing a disguised payload before running it.

patterns.name: Discovery to Scheduled Task Persistence
patterns.description: Process enumeration (possibly checking for security tools) followed by scheduled-task persistence.

patterns.name: Discovery to Registry Persistence
patterns.description: Host fingerprinting followed directly by registry-based persistence, without an intermediate execution stage.

patterns.name: Credential Access to Evidence Destruction
patterns.description: Failed logon attempts followed by clearing of the Security event log, consistent with an attacker covering their tracks after a credential-guessing attempt.

patterns.name: Evasion to Persistence (Hidden Extensions then Registry Run Key)
patterns.description: File-extension hiding followed directly by registry-based persistence, without an intermediate execution stage.

patterns.name: Suspicious Account Tampering (Rare Failure Code)
patterns.description: A failed logon with an uncommon failure reason (disabled account, restricted hours, unauthorized workstation, or trust failure), distinct from ordinary bad-password attempts.

patterns.name: Command Injection: Web Request to Spawned Process
patterns.description: A request to a known command-injection-vulnerable web endpoint, immediately followed by the web server process spawning a shell or system utility on the same host -- the web-log and endpoint evidence for the same real intrusion, correlated together.

response_action.target_stage_contains: Suspicious Child Process Spawned by Web Server

stages.match_contains: Suspicious Child Process Spawned by Web Server

patterns.name: SQL Injection (Web Application)
patterns.description: A request matching known SQL Injection syntax against a web application endpoint.

patterns.name: Path Traversal / Local File Inclusion (Web Application)
patterns.description: A request attempting to read files outside the web application's intended directory.

patterns.name: Cross-Site Scripting (Web Application)
patterns.description: A request containing an unescaped script or event-handler payload reflected by the web application.

patterns.name: Security Event Log Cleared (Anti-Forensics)
patterns.description: The Security event log was cleared. Reported as a standalone incident regardless of surrounding events, since this action alone destroys evidence and warrants investigation on its own merits.
